advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that a mid-evaluation exception on an under-floor REPEAT-FIX diff still records escalation_reason='repeat-fix' and repeat_fix_priors in the recovery path.
evidence: bugfix_size_gate.py:388 recovery block: `non_test, reason, priors = escalation_for_diff(diff_text or "", repo_root=repo_root)`

tests/unit/test_bugfix_size_gate_ad0d.py:374 `test_classifier_exception_abstains_indeterminate` uses `diff_text=_file_diff("src/rebar/big.py", added=_BIG)` (size floor) and asserts only verdict/blocking/advisory and `coverage[...]['verdict'] == 'error'`
ABSENCE: no test drives the classifier-exception recovery path with a repeat-fix (under-floor) diff and asserts escalation_reason == 'repeat-fix' / non-empty repeat_fix_priors in the coverage record
advisory.finding: The gate's exception-recovery branch re-derives escalation_reason/repeat_fix_priors from escalation_for_diff, but no test exercises that recovery path for a REPEAT-FIX diff. test_classifier_exception_abstains_indeterminate only injects a failure on a size-floor diff (_BIG) and asserts verdict/bucket, never asserting the newly-added escalation_reason or repeat_fix_priors keys survive the recovery path. A regression in the recovery-block re-derivation of the new keys would not be caught.
scenarios: A future edit breaks the re-derivation of escalation_reason/priors in the except-branch; the size-only recovery test still passes.

ABSENCE: no assertion that the blocking finding for a size+repeat-fix change names both the over-floor clause and the prior SHAs
advisory.finding: The `size+repeat-fix` teaching-finding text branch (_escalation_clause: `f"{size}, and {repeat}" if priors else size`) is exercised but never asserted. test_both_signals_are_reported_together asserts only escalation_reason=='size+repeat-fix', and test_the_teaching_finding_names_the_prior_fixes covers only the repeat-fix-only clause, so a regression in the combined finding text would go unnoticed.
scenarios: The combined finding text is later broken (e.g. priors dropped from the over-floor branch) with no failing test.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Record in the coverage record whether the repeat-fix history walk actually completed (e.g. a `repeat_fix_checked`/`repeat_fix_error` flag) so an inconclusive walk is distinguishable from a genuine no-escalation.
evidence: repeat_fix.py:52-53 `if proc.returncode != 0: return None` — a failed walk yields empty priors, identical to 'clean, no priors'
bugfix_size_gate.py:288-290 `except Exception: logger.warning(...); return False, []` — a predicate fault is logged but the verdict/coverage record shows only the size reason

bugfix_size_gate.py:406-407 the coverage keys `escalation_reason`/`repeat_fix_priors` carry no 'repeat-fix check did not run / was inconclusive' state, so an absent escalation cannot be told apart from an unread history
dropped.finding: The repeat-fix predicate is fail-open on any git error/timeout (`_git` returns None on nonzero returncode or exception; `_repeat_fix_verdict` swallows exceptions), and the resulting coverage record records only `escalation_reason` (e.g. "size" or "") with no marker that the history walk was inconclusive. A gate run where git timed out or the base_ref was unreadable produces the same coverage/verdict as a run that read full history and found no repeat fix — the two cannot be distinguished after the fact.

ticket 1dd5 remediation comment: 'Running it took ~25 minutes and reported 644 bug-fix commits'
dropped.finding: `--repeat-fix` invokes `escalation_for_diff` per commit, which runs `repeat_fix_escalates` — one `git log --no-merges --since --until <base_ref> -- <path>` subprocess per distinct non-test path per commit. Over `origin/main` (644+ bug-fix commits per the ticket) this is thousands of serial git subprocess invocations; the ticket itself records the run taking ~25 minutes.
